name: North Carolina

sales.rateNote: General State rate of 4.75%. Every county levies local taxes under Articles 39, 40 and 42 totalling 2.00%; some counties add 0.25% (Article 46) and some a 0.50% transit tax. Total county rates are published by NCDOR (current table effective July 1, 2026).

local.levies: counties (Articles 39, 40 and 42 in all 100 counties; optional Article 46 quarter-cent) and county public transportation (transit) taxes under Article 43
local.capNote: Local rate increases must be enacted and levied at least 90 days before their effective date.

groceries.note: Qualifying food is exempt from the State and transit rates but subject to a flat 2.00% local rate statewide. Prepared food, candy, soft drinks, dietary supplements and food from vending machines (non-qualifying food) bear the full State, local and transit rates.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable tangible personal property at the general State and local rates.

otherRates.note: 3% State rate with a maximum tax of $1,500 per boat (jet skis, kayaks and canoes included); local and transit rates do not apply.
General State rate applied to 50% of the sales price; local and transit rates do not apply.
General State rate only, maximum tax $2,500 per aircraft.
Flat 2.00% local rate; State and transit rates do not apply.

useTax.note: Consumer use tax is due on taxable items bought without North Carolina tax; individuals filing Form D-400 report it on the income tax return, others on Form E-554 (boats, aircraft and 2% food always on E-554). Applicable local and transit rates are added.

facts.text: Since July 1, 2026 Mecklenburg County levies an additional local sales and use tax, changing its combined rate.
Groceries are not fully tax-free: a 2% local rate applies to qualifying food in every county, reported on the '2% Food Rate' line of Form E-500.
Boats are capped at $1,500 of tax; surfboards, paddle boards and windsurfers are not 'boats' and pay the full general rate.
Drugs required by federal law to be dispensed only on prescription, over-the-counter drugs sold on prescription, and insulin are exempt.
Forty-eight counties levy the optional 0.25% Article 46 tax; the 0.50% Article 43 transit tax is levied only in Durham, Mecklenburg, Orange and Wake counties.
A prepared food item is food sold heated, two or more foods combined by the retailer, or food sold with utensils provided by the retailer.

property.levied: local: counties, municipalities and special districts set tax rates per $100 of appraised value; county assessors appraise and list property. Real property is listed in the county where it is located.

assessment.text: The tax bill equals the county appraisal (market value as of the county's last reappraisal) divided by 100 and multiplied by the combined county and municipal/district rate. Reappraisal years vary by county and are published by NCDOR.

homestead.name: Elderly or Disabled Homestead Exclusion
homestead.text: Excludes the greater of the first $25,000 or 50% of the appraised value of the permanent residence of an owner aged 65+ or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income does not exceed $38,800 (2026 tax year; $39,900 for 2027).
homestead.applyBy: Form AV-9 filed with the county assessor by June 1.

otherRelief.name: Circuit Breaker Property Tax Deferment
otherRelief.text: For owners 65+ or totally disabled who have owned and occupied the home five full years: taxes are limited to 4% of income up to $38,800, or 5% of income up to $58,200 (2026); the excess is deferred. Cannot be combined with the other two exclusions.

otherRelief.name: Disabled Veteran Exclusion
otherRelief.text: Excludes up to the first $45,000 of appraised value of the permanent residence of a disabled veteran; no age or income limit; also available to an unremarried surviving spouse.

facts.text: The regular listing period for property is the month of January; counties may extend it, and individual extensions can run to April 15.
Under 'Tag and Tax Together', vehicle property tax is paid to NCDMV with the registration renewal, not to the county.
NCDOR's official example: a $200,000 home taxed at a combined 0.865 per $100 owes $1,730.
Income limit for the elderly/disabled exclusion rises from $38,800 (2026) to $39,900 (2027); circuit breaker upper limit $59,850 in 2027.
